name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, including 1,800 in DR Congo, mostly in the conflict-hit east
state: WHO said on 4 Nov that DR Congo has recorded more than 60,000 cholera cases and 1,800 deaths in 2026, a fatality rate of about 3%, concentrated in North and South Kivu and spreading along the Congo River towards Kinshasa (Vidal, citing AFP). WHO said on 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people died of cholera worldwide in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa (Ahram Online, citing AFP). ECDC's 27 Oct update lists large outbreaks in Nigeria, DR Congo, South Sudan and Yemen. Searches on 27 Nov found no sign these outbreaks are ending, so the Alert holds.
for_you: Risk to UK residents is very low. Travellers to affected areas should follow NHS Fit for Travel and FCDO advice on safe water, food hygiene and vaccination.
rubric_hit: Alert: large outbreak with high mortality in a conflict zone, DR Congo 1,800 deaths, fatality rate about 3% (WHO)

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
